question: When the polynomial \(x^3-2\) is divided by the polynomial \(x^2-2,\) the remainder is
solution:
Multiplying the divisor by \(x\) produces the leading term \(x^3\), so subtracting this multiple reveals the remainder:
\[x^3-2-x(x^2-2)=x^3-2-x^3+2x=2x-2.\]
Thus
\[x^3-2=x(x^2-2)+(2x-2).\]
The remaining polynomial has degree one, which is less than the divisor's degree two, so division is complete. The remainder is \(2x-2\), choice E.
